episode_title: All the questions you wanted to ask during GAAD – but didn’t get the chance
question: What percentage of the UK population has a permanent disability or progressive impairment?
transcript_excerpt: About 25% of the UK population have a permanent disability, and an additional 15% have a progressive impairment, which means approximately four out of 10 people may be consuming your digital products or attending your events and meetings.

episode_title: All the questions you wanted to ask during GAAD – but didn’t get the chance
question: How many people in the UK need captions compared to sign language interpretation services?
transcript_excerpt: About 11 million people in the UK need captions for difficulty hearing, while only 25,000 people need sign interpretation, which is why most organizations provide captions but not BSL interpretation at events due to cost and demand differences.

episode_title: All the questions you wanted to ask during GAAD – but didn’t get the chance
question: What is BS 8878 and why is it significant for digital accessibility?
transcript_excerpt: BS 8878 is the British standard for accessibility. It became one of the first digital standards in the world that actually consulted with autistic people, a group regularly excluded from accessibility standards, after an autistic expert provided detailed adjustment requirements for a meeting consultation.

episode_title: All the questions you wanted to ask during GAAD – but didn’t get the chance
question: What are the three main audiences for accessible events and meetings in organizations?
transcript_excerpt: The three audiences are: customers or external attendees at large events; clients or stakeholders in business presentations; and internal staff members with disabilities who need all organizational communications and meetings to be accessible to them.

episode_title: All the questions you wanted to ask during GAAD – but didn’t get the chance
question: What is the recommended minimum approach for organizations with limited budgets to make events accessible?
transcript_excerpt: Start with captions first, as they help the most people and have the lowest cost barrier. You can turn on automated captions in Zoom or even PowerPoint presentations without paying additional fees, though human captioning is more accurate than AI for specialized content.
